standards: WHATWG HTML Standard 13.2.5 tokenization (including the named character reference table and processing-instruction states)
WHATWG HTML Standard 13.2.6 tree construction (all insertion modes, adoption agency, foster parenting, foreign content, templates) and 13.4 fragment parsing
Selectors Level 4 (type, universal, id, class, attribute selectors with the i and s flags, the four combinators, selector lists)
HTML Standard list of case-insensitive attribute values for attribute selectors
licence_note: The parser is written from the standard's text, not from html5ever, scraper or any browser. The html5lib-tests tokenizer and tree-construction data are MIT (Copyright html5lib contributors) and are committed with their LICENSE. Named character references are generated from the WHATWG entities.json (entities.tsv).

scope.scripting: enabled (noscript holds raw text, as html5ever and browsers with scripting on); no script is ever executed
scope.template: a template element's contents are a detached fragment, so they are not matched by selectors or counted in text (the standard and browsers); the donor kept them as a child of the template
scope.selectors: pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements and namespace prefixes are rejected when the selector is parsed, never silently unmatched; ids and classes always compare case-sensitively
scope.unsupported_in_the_standard_text_followe: declarative shadow roots and template-for patching are not implemented (such templates are plain templates); the selectedcontent cloning of customizable select is not implemented (4 html5lib cases skipped by name)
scope.select: the select element has no insertion mode in the current standard: its children are parsed in body, with select a scope boundary
scope.depth: the stack of open elements is iterative and counts the elements that scope checks look for, so 60000 nested elements parse in 0.1 seconds in a debug build
